statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains below the block threshold because the Nasdaq-100 advance is still two-way, while Stress stays high on conflicting cross-asset signals into quarter-end index marks and a scheduled post-close memory-sector report.
recommendation: Tail is in the watch band and below the block threshold. The flagged window spans the 20:00Z cash close through 22:00Z, covering final-day quarter-end index marks and the post-close memory-sector fiscal Q4 report in thinning liquidity.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a two-way gain after softer August PCE, with quarter-end marks and a post-close memory report as the immediate checkpoints
body: The Nasdaq-100 trades at 30,560.07, up 220.74 points or 0.73%, inside a 30,415.16-30,630.45 range after opening at 30,421.68 against a 30,339.33 previous close. NQ futures at 30,841.00 (+0.74%) first traded down to 30,512.25 from a 30,657.25 open, a retracement of roughly 145 points, then recovered to about 64 points below the 30,905.50 session high. That completed retracement, the index sitting some 70 points under its own session high, and VIX at 15.95 below the 16.04 prior close and off its 16.32 high, together indicate that mean reversion is still functioning rather than a persistent one-way path. Tail therefore stays in the watch band. August PCE printed softer than expected at 3.4% year over year against 3.7% anticipated, with core PCE at 3.0% versus 3.3% and core PCE month over month at 0.2% versus 0.3%. Repricing has been orderly. New York Fed President Williams saying there is no need for urgency has cut implied October hike odds to roughly 35%, from above 70% a week earlier and 50% the previous day, with December now the more likely venue for any further move. Stress remains high because cross-asset signals conflict with the equity advance. The 10-year yield rose four basis points to 5.29% despite the softer inflation data, having traded a 5.20-5.31 range. WTI gained 1.3% to about $90.55 and Brent rose about 2% toward $98 on continued uncertainty around U.S.-Iran negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz. Leadership is narrow, with the Dow down 0.46% while the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.83%, and single-stock dispersion is elevated. Supporting releases were firmer than the inflation print: ADP employment came in at 90,000 against 70,000 expected, final Q2 GDP growth was 2.2% versus 1.5%, and the Chicago PMI beat sharply at 58.8 against 51.2. The main unresolved forward item is a memory-sector fiscal Q4 report scheduled after the 20:00Z cash close, arriving alongside final-day quarter-end index marks. The sector carries meaningful index weight and market attention is on whether gross margins stay elevated and whether memory demand keeps outpacing supply. That is a credible delayed second-information-wave mechanism into thin liquidity, so it is reflected in Stress and in a narrow flagged window rather than in a Tail block, because no post-print price path has been observed yet. The shared Finviz context file was collected at 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z with a partial collection status and its futures and calendar sections unavailable. At roughly 20 hours old it is well beyond the 90-minute freshness limit, so it was treated as stale and not used as evidence; all cross-asset, breadth and calendar inputs above come from independent current research.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours carry published Claude assessments. Tail eased from 20 to 15 across the overnight and European hours as volatility decayed, then rebuilt from 15 to a 23 peak through the U.S. morning around the PCE release and the quarter-end approach, easing to 22 and then 21 in the last two hours. Stress held in the high band throughout, between 65 and 72. Mode was mixed for most of the window, with a short normal stretch late on September 29.
outlookSummary: Tail is projected to hold in the watch band through the 20:00Z cash close, quarter-end index marks and the post-close memory-sector report, peaking at 24 between 20:00Z and 22:00Z without crossing the block threshold, because no post-print price path is observed yet and scheduled event importance is treated as a Stress input. Tail then decays into the low band across the Asian and European sessions as the calendar empties and the quarter turn removes rebalancing pressure, reaching a 16 floor between 04:00Z and 06:00Z. It rebuilds to 20 for the 12:30Z jobless-claims slot, 21 for the 13:30Z cash open, and a 23 second-day peak at the 14:00Z ISM manufacturing release, before easing to 19 late in the U.S. afternoon ahead of non-farm payrolls on October 2. Confidence drifts from 88 to 80 with forecast distance.
